summary: Completed backend + frontend regression for trusted-proxy rate limiting, hero/image responsiveness, mobile menu behavior, and contact form UI states on public preview.

minor.issue: Shared preview traffic frequently saturates the 5/600 bucket before tests start, causing legitimate rate-limit tests to skip (expected in shared env, not a code defect).

action_items: Optional: keep one dedicated QA window/IP (or isolated bucket namespace) if deterministic public rate-limit verification is required every run.
Optional hardening review: confirm ingress/proxy forwarding policy still aligns with TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS assumptions in production deployment.
critical_code_review_comments: Trusted-proxy parser tests pass: right-to-left traversal selects first untrusted hop and ignores fake leftmost header values.

Mobile menu behavior now matches expected UX: Escape closes, X closes, same-route nav click closes, focus returns to trigger, background remains locked while open, and short-height sheet supports native internal scroll.
Hero image is masked/feathered and stable with no horizontal overflow at 320/390/768/1024/1440/1920; source paths resolve correctly.
Contact form success/reset/error flows verified with browser-level intercepted responses only (no MOCKED backend API).
All audited interactive elements across /faq, /services, /how-we-work, /about, /contact had data-testid and no duplicate IDs detected.
seed_data_creation: Yes. API tests created transient status records and at least one real enquiry during initial backend run before limiter saturation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Latest playwright evidence confirms mobile sheet and hero fixes are working on preview URL. Contact flow interception passed using current selectors (contact-input-*, contact-client-type-bookkeeping, contact-support-monthly, form-success/form-error). Backend full suite result: 9 passed, 5 skipped due shared rate-limit saturation.
rca of the issue: No new product bug reproduced in this run. Prior flakiness was environment-driven: shared ingress traffic can pre-consume rate-limit slots, leading to early 429/skip behavior in public-preview tests.
